name: Gale Levin
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I have a drawer of damaged linings where the damaged side is the lovely one.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Gale by a small Monday habit. Gale pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I paid for a matching cuff lining on condition the customer never learns my name. He guessed from the fabric.
appearance: Gale has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a narrow-striped sweater with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. In conversation Gale looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Gale treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To fit the donated lining without attaching a personal debt.
family: Kit Curtis is Gale’s stepsibling. Gale makes room at the table. Kit brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Three minutes at the bridge*, Kit says, “I have been paying taxi fares with credit. I showed the crew my actual monthly statement before the vote.”
connections: Isla Osei. They decide which expensive additions the applicant can decline.
